title: E-commerce Platform: Complete Architecture
description: Design an e-commerce platform with monolith and microservice architectures using React, ASP.NET Core, Azure, and AWS.

data.text: Design an e-commerce platform that supports browsing a product catalog, searching and filtering products, adding items to a cart, checkout with multiple payment methods, order tracking, inventory management, and personalized recommendations. The system must handle seasonal traffic spikes, maintain consistent inventory counts during flash sales, and provide an admin dashboard for managing products, orders, and customer data.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Browse products by category, brand, price range, and attributes with faceted search
Manage a shopping cart with quantity updates, discounts, and saved carts
Checkout flow with address selection, shipping calculation, and multiple payment options
Track order status from placement through shipment and delivery
Reserve inventory during checkout to prevent overselling
Restock and manage product inventory with low-stock alerts
Generate product recommendations based on browsing history and purchases
Admin interface to manage products, categories, orders, and customer support tickets
Customer reviews, ratings, and wishlist functionality

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: 99.9% availability during normal and peak traffic
Sub-200ms product listing and search results
Sub-2-second checkout completion after payment authorization
Inventory updates visible across all channels within 100ms
Shopping cart syncs across devices without conflicts
Search handles 10,000+ queries per second during sales
Product images served from CDN with 99.99% cache hit ratio
Database sharding for orders table at 100 million records

data.text: Start with a monolithic ASP.NET Core application with MVC or Razor Pages for the storefront and an API for cart and checkout operations. Entity Framework Core manages the product catalog, cart, orders, and inventory in a relational database. The monolith is the fastest path to launch a full-featured e-commerce site with consistent ACID transactions for orders and inventory.

terms.term: - Entity Framework Core for data access
- Azure SQL Database or AWS RDS for relational data
- Built-in DI, logging, and health checks
- Azure App Service or AWS EC2/ECS
- Azure Blob Storage or AWS S3 for file assets
- Azure Monitor or AWS CloudWatch for logging
- Single database with tables for all domains

data.text: When catalog size, traffic, and order volume grow, split the monolith into microservices. Catalog Service handles product search and browsing with Elasticsearch or Redis for caching. Cart Service manages per-user cart state with Redis for fast access. Order Service orchestrates checkout with the saga pattern. Inventory Service owns stock levels and reservation logic. Recommendation Service generates personalized suggestions. User Service handles profiles, addresses, and authentication.

items: Catalog Service: Indexes products in Elasticsearch, serves search and faceted filters, manages categories and attributes, and caches top-selling products in Redis.
Cart Service: Manages per-user shopping carts with Redis for fast reads, merges anonymous carts on login, and applies promo codes and discounts.
Order Service: Orchestrates checkout using the saga pattern, creates order records, and coordinates inventory reservation and payment capture.
Payment Service: Handles payment authorization, capture, and refund events via payment gateway integration with idempotent retry logic.
Inventory Service: Tracks stock levels across warehouses, reserves units during checkout, releases reservations on cancellation or timeout, and emits low-stock alerts.
Recommendation Service: Generates personalized product suggestions using collaborative filtering and real-time browsing signals from Kafka or event streams.
User Service: Manages customer profiles, shipping addresses, authentication, and order history views with separate read-optimized projections.

data.title: When to Choose Microservices?
data.text: Start with a monolith. Split into microservices only when you have clear scaling bottlenecks, independent deployment needs, or team boundaries that justify the operational overhead.

data.title: Summary
points: A E-commerce Platform system requires both simple and scalable designs
Monolith is fastest to validate; microservices are for scale
React + ASP.NET Core provides a robust full-stack foundation
Azure Cosmos DB and Amazon DynamoDB are strong choices for distributed data
Always design for failure: retries, circuit breakers, and fallbacks
data.takeaway: E-commerce Platform is a distributed system. Start simple, then scale horizontally with microservices, caching, and managed cloud services.
